architecture.new_modular_config_role: stable module membership, practice identity, content status, version, completion, and counterpart policy

module_completion.internal_review_build: A module completes after every runnable practice currently listed for that module is completed. Gated and blocked records never count.
module_completion.production: No production completion policy is authorized until practices are individually promoted to launch_eligible and Donald approves the required subset.

legacy_day_migration.existing_explicit_module_7_or_8_records: Preserve as legacy historical records without coercing them into completion of the new Module 7 or Module 8 curriculum. Do not delete or rewrite the stored record.

counterpart_and_voice.provider_or_audio_failure: Preserve visible text and fail closed without regenerating the turn.
counterpart_and_voice.internal_review_audio: Provider-generated TTS is acceptable for internal testing with visible text fallback.
counterpart_and_voice.production_audio: Voice choice, pronunciation, and reusable audio require separate approval.

safety.safety_contract_fields_in_curriculum: Authoring exclusions and content-review gates, not authorization to classify ordinary spoken content or replace counterpart roleplay at runtime.
safety.safety_sensitive_draft_practices: Internal review only; launch_eligible remains false.
safety.future_runtime_safety_change: Requires a separate product decision, threat model, false-positive review, deterministic tests, and approved user-facing copy.

duration.legacy_duration_fields: Leave untouched in the legacy migration source during this implementation; never display or copy them into the modular config.

content_visibility.internal_review: All 43 runnable practices are accessible and visibly marked as review content in non-production/internal builds.
content_visibility.gated: Not runnable; display only in internal curriculum inventory, not as a tappable practice.
content_visibility.blocked: Not runnable and never simulated with fake mechanics.
content_visibility.production: Only separately promoted launch_eligible practices may appear to real users.

missing_package_artifacts.policy: Use the audited current pilotCurriculum.json as the exact machine source for approved Days 2–8 and the Markdown package as the human authority. Do not fabricate missing audio or fixture artifacts.

implementation_stages.name: Schema and config validation
deliverables: Add versioned modular config and validators.
Preserve legacy pilotCurriculum.json unchanged as migration source.
Add stable practice IDs, module membership, statuses, content versions, counterpart policy, and completion declarations.
Prove all 53 IDs are unique and every module is revisitable.

implementation_stages.name: Read-only migration and identity correction
deliverables: Map historical day completion to practice evidence idempotently.
Remove duplicate Day 8 ownership from new module inference.
Preserve ambiguous and explicit legacy records without coercion.

implementation_stages.name: Internal full-curriculum review build
deliverables: Wire 43 runnable review practices into the existing paid flow.
Keep two gated and eight blocked practices non-runnable.
Use contextual counterpart identity and immutable same-turn retry.
Expose no review draft to production users.

implementation_stages.name: Deterministic QA and evidence
deliverables: Run migration, restart, safety-boundary, comparison, contextual identity, persistence, Progress, and frozen-parity tests.
Generate route-mounted visual state evidence after tests pass.
Perform provider, audio, microphone, and native-device QA separately.

implementation_stages.name: Production promotion
deliverables: Revise content versions without changing stable IDs where behavior is unchanged.
Promote practices individually only after content, safety, audio, and product approval.

modules.title: Get to the Point
modules.promise: Organize what you mean, identify the point that matters, and say it without burying it under explanations.
modules.completion_capability: I can identify the job, state one point, and keep it present when the conversation branches.

practices.title: Give the conversation one job
practices.preview: Decide what this conversation is for, then whether now is a good time to have it.
what_you_will_practice: Name the job of the conversation.
Decide whether to continue, narrow the topic, return later, or move it to writing.
lesson_cards: A conversation gets harder when you’re asking it to do five things at once. Choose the one job it needs to do today.
The job might be to understand, decide, ask for something, repair what happened, set a limit, or share something hard.
Then look at the conditions. You can shrink the topic, move it to another time, or put it in writing.
You don’t have to finish a conversation just because you started it.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which version gives the conversation one clear job?
options: I need you to understand why I’m upset, apologize, agree I’m right, and decide bedtime tonight.
I want us to decide who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday.
feedback: A is carrying four jobs. B asks for one decision: who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday.
B asks for a single decision: who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday.

preset_scenario.heading: Bedtime needs an owner
preset_scenario.briefing: You want to decide who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday.
preset_scenario.user_opening_objective: Open by saying what you want decided.
preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I can talk, but I have to leave in ten minutes.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: You have ten minutes. Narrow the topic, set a time to finish, or move the conversation to text.

may_evaluate: The timing, scope, or channel choice is usable.

retry.direction: Use the same ten-minute limit. Change only the part Hope named.

practices.transfer_cue: Next time something big is coming, ask yourself what you want the conversation to settle.

practices.title: Separate what happened from the story
practices.preview: Say what happened so another person could point to the same event.
lesson_cards: Start with something another person could point to: what was said, done, or agreed.
Stop before you turn what you think it means into a fact about them.
Your feelings can stay in. Leave out the verdict about what the event says about them.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which one starts with something that happened?
options: You don’t care how exhausted I am.
I handled bedtime alone four nights this week after we agreed to split it.
feedback: A turns a motive into a fact. B gives a count and names the agreement.
B gives the other person something specific to answer.

preset_scenario.briefing: You want to describe what this week has actually looked like.
preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What actually happened this week?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Say what happened this week in a sentence or two. Stop before you say what it means about the other person.

may_evaluate: No motive or character claim is presented as fact.
may_not_infer: that a feeling was expressed incorrectly

retry.direction: Give one thing that happened this week. Stop before you say what it proves.

practices.transfer_cue: Prepare one current example for the real conversation. Don’t build a historical case file.

practices.title: Keep one point in the room
practices.preview: Stay with your point after an objection you need to address.
lesson_cards: Pick the point you want to keep clear, even when the conversation gets uncomfortable.
One example is enough. Stack up three and the other person answers the stack instead of the point.
When the other person objects, say you heard it. Then go back to the same point.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which one is easier to stay on?
options: This is about bedtime, the dishes, your phone, your mother visiting, and how we never spend time together.
The point I need to keep clear is that bedtime needs an owner, not another list I manage.
feedback: A opens five issues at once. B leaves one thing to answer.
B keeps one point in view without building a case.

preset_scenario.briefing: You want bedtime to have a clear owner instead of another list you manage.
preset_scenario.user_opening_objective: Say the point once. Then hold it after the objection.
preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I do bedtime when I can. Work has been all over the place.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Respond to the part about work, then come back to bedtime. Leave the other issues for later.

may_evaluate: At most one supporting example is used.
The same point remains after resistance.
may_not_infer: a universal word limit for a good answer

retry.direction: Answer the work concern briefly, then return to the bedtime request.

practices.transfer_cue: Say your one point out loud before the real conversation.

practices.title: Acknowledge once, then return
practices.preview: Respond to what matters without following every new branch.
lesson_cards: Being responsive doesn’t mean following every new branch.
Acknowledge the part that matters. Then return to the request, boundary, or decision you started with.
If the new concern needs its own conversation, give it a real return point instead of arguing about both at once.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response acknowledges the concern and keeps the original decision visible?
options: Okay, never mind. We can talk about my tone instead.
You’re right that I sounded sharp. I want to address that, and I also want to finish deciding who owns bedtime.
feedback: A drops the original decision. B acknowledges the concern and returns to it.
B makes room for the concern without losing the original decision.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: You’re talking about bedtime, but the way you brought it up was unfair.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Acknowledge what needs acknowledging, then return to the bedtime decision.

retry.direction: Acknowledge once, then return to the one decision.

practices.transfer_cue: Prepare one return phrase that sounds like something you would actually say.

practices.title: Stop when the point is clear
practices.preview: Use enough detail to make the point understandable without building a case file.
lesson_cards: More examples can make a clear point harder to answer.
Use one current example when it helps. Then stop and leave room for a response.
If the point is already understandable, another example usually changes the conversation into a trial.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response gives enough evidence without turning into a case?
options: You did it Tuesday, last weekend, when your parents visited, and three times last month.
I handled bedtime alone four nights this week after we agreed to split it.
feedback: A keeps adding history. B gives one current example the other person can answer.
B gives enough detail to make the point discussable, then stops.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I understand this week was rough. Why are you bringing up everything from last month too?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Use one current example and return to the decision you need now.

may_evaluate: One current example supports the point.
Historical evidence does not replace the current request.

retry.direction: Use one current example, then return to what you need decided now.

practices.transfer_cue: Before a difficult conversation, choose the one example you actually need.

modules.title: Make a Clear Ask
modules.promise: Turn a vague need, frustration, or desired quality into something another person can actually answer.
modules.completion_capability: I can make a specific request without turning the answer into a test of whether the other person cares.

practices.title: Find the ask inside the frustration
practices.preview: Find the action or decision hiding underneath a broad complaint.
lesson_cards: Frustration often points to something you want changed, but it doesn’t always name the change.
Ask what action, decision, or ownership would make the concern discussable.
Keep the feeling and concern. Replace the test of character with something that can be answered.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which version turns the frustration into something discussable?
options: I need you to care more about this family.
I want us to decide who owns bedtime on Tuesday and Thursday.
feedback: A asks for a quality. B names the decision hidden inside the frustration.
B turns the frustration into one decision the other person can answer.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What are you asking me to do differently?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Name the action or decision underneath the frustration.

may_evaluate: One action or decision can be identified.

retry.direction: Name the action or decision hiding underneath the frustration.

practices.transfer_cue: When you hear yourself asking for a quality, look for the action underneath it.

practices.title: Make one answerable request
practices.preview: Ask for one next step the other person can answer.
lesson_cards: Turn the concern into a next step the other person can accept, decline, or change.
Say what, who, and when. Skip the parts that don’t matter.
A request leaves room for an answer. It isn’t a loyalty test, and a yes isn’t guaranteed.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which one can the other person answer?
options: I need you to care more and show up for this family.
Can you own bedtime every Tuesday and Thursday, including pajamas, teeth, and lights out?
feedback: A asks for a quality. B asks for a job, a person, and two nights.
B gives the other person a clear request they can accept, decline, or change.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: Tuesday might work. Thursday I’m at work late.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Respond to the Thursday conflict. Adjust the nights or ask what would work.
preset_scenario.user_opening_objective: Ask who will do what and on which nights.

may_evaluate: One action or decision is identifiable.

retry.direction: Ask who will do what and when. Leave room for a no or a different plan.

practices.transfer_cue: Try the request in a smaller conversation, or save it for the conversation you have in mind.

practices.title: Make ownership and timing clear
practices.preview: Make the next step specific enough that both people know who owns it and when it happens.
lesson_cards: A clear request makes ownership visible.
Add timing when timing changes whether the request can actually happen.
Skip details that don’t affect the answer.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which request makes ownership and timing clear?
options: Can you help more with bedtime?
Can you own the full bedtime routine Tuesday and Thursday this week?
feedback: A leaves the task and timing open. B names the owner, task, and nights.
B makes the requested ownership and timing visible.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What exactly would I be responsible for?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Name the owner, the full task, and the timing that matters.

retry.direction: Name the owner, the action, and the timing that matters.

practices.transfer_cue: Before making a request, check whether the owner and timing are actually clear.

practices.title: Leave room for an answer
practices.preview: Make the request without turning one answer into proof of whether the person cares.
lesson_cards: A request can be accepted, declined, clarified, or changed.
Pressure begins when only one answer is allowed and every other answer becomes a character test.
Keep the need visible without pretending the other person has already agreed.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which request leaves room for a real answer?
options: If you cared, you would take both nights.
Can you take Tuesday and Thursday, or tell me which two nights could work?
feedback: A makes agreement a test of caring. B keeps the request clear and allows a workable response.
B leaves room for yes, no, clarification, or another plan.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I can’t promise both nights every week.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Keep the request clear while leaving room for a constraint or alternative.

may_evaluate: The request permits more than one legitimate answer.
may_not_infer: whether the request is morally owed

retry.direction: Keep the request clear and leave room for a no, constraint, or alternative.

practices.transfer_cue: Listen for care tests such as “if you wanted to” and replace them with the actual request.

practices.title: Adjust after a real constraint
practices.preview: Respond to a practical concern without dropping the need or forcing the original plan.
lesson_cards: A real constraint does not automatically erase the request.
Answer the part that affects feasibility, then adjust the plan or ask what would work.
Changing the plan is different from abandoning the need.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response works with the constraint without losing the request?
options: Fine. Forget the whole thing.
If Thursday runs late, which other night can you own from start to finish?
feedback: A abandons the request. B adjusts the timing while keeping the ownership need visible.
B responds to the constraint and asks for a workable alternative.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: Thursday I’m at work late.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Respond to the conflict and ask for a workable alternative.

may_not_infer: whether the constraint is an excuse

retry.direction: Address the constraint, then ask what workable alternative keeps the request intact.

practices.transfer_cue: When a real constraint appears, adjust what can change without losing what still matters.

practices.title: Close with the actual next step
practices.preview: End with what was decided, what remains open, and when it will be revisited.
lesson_cards: A useful conversation can still end without a reliable next step.
Name what was actually decided. Do not inflate partial agreement.
If something remains open, say when or how it will be revisited.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which close makes the current decision visible?
options: Okay, I guess we’ll both try harder.
You’ll own Tuesday bedtime. We’ll check Thursday on Wednesday night.
feedback: A does not name an owner or next check. B states the agreement and the unresolved part.
B makes the actual decision and next check visible.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I can commit to Tuesday. I need to check Thursday.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: State what was decided, what remains open, and when you will revisit it.

may_evaluate: The unresolved point and next check are visible.

retry.direction: State what was decided, what remains open, and when you will revisit it.

practices.transfer_cue: Close one coordination conversation by naming the owner, next action, or unresolved point.

modules.title: Start the Conversation
modules.promise: Bring something up clearly without ambushing, accusing, or delivering the entire case in the opening.
modules.completion_capability: I can begin clearly enough that the other person knows what we are discussing and why.

practices.title: Choose timing, scope, and channel
practices.preview: Decide whether this conversation should happen now, later, or somewhere else.
lesson_cards: Before you open the conversation, check whether the conditions can hold the job you are asking it to do.
You can narrow the topic, choose another time, or move the conversation to writing.
Delaying with a real return plan is different from making the issue disappear.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response makes a usable timing choice?
options: We have to settle all of this before you leave.
This needs more than ten minutes. Can we talk after bedtime at 8:30?
feedback: A forces the full conversation into unusable timing. B names a concrete return.
B keeps the conversation alive while choosing better conditions.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I have to leave in ten minutes.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Choose whether to narrow the topic, set a return, or change the channel.

may_evaluate: The timing, scope, or channel choice is usable.

retry.direction: Choose a usable scope, return time, or channel for the same conversation.

practices.transfer_cue: Before opening something important, check whether the time and channel fit the job.

practices.title: Name what this is about
practices.preview: Let the other person know the topic before you deliver the whole case.
lesson_cards: A clear opening tells the other person what conversation they are entering.
Name the topic before adding examples or conclusions.
The topic can be brief: bedtime ownership, the comment at dinner, or how a decision will be made.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which opening names the topic?
options: We need to talk about everything that has been going wrong.
Can we talk about who owns bedtime on weeknights?
feedback: A leaves the topic open-ended. B names the decision under discussion.
B makes the topic clear before adding the case.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What do you want to talk about?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Name the topic in one sentence without opening every related issue.

retry.direction: Name the topic in one sentence without adding the whole case.

practices.transfer_cue: Prepare the sentence that tells the other person what conversation you are opening.

practices.title: Use one current example
practices.preview: Give one example that makes the topic concrete without prosecuting the person.
lesson_cards: One current example can make an opening easier to understand.
Use what happened, not a verdict about what it proves.
Stop before the example turns into a list of every prior offense.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which example makes the topic concrete?
options: You always leave everything to me.
I handled bedtime alone four nights this week after we agreed to split it.
feedback: A gives a global verdict. B gives one current event connected to the topic.
B makes the topic concrete without turning it into a character claim.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What makes you want to change this now?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Give one current example and stop before explaining what it proves about the person.

may_evaluate: One current observable example is present.

retry.direction: Give one current example, then stop before turning it into a verdict.

practices.transfer_cue: Choose the one current example that will help the other person understand the topic.

practices.title: Say the impact without claiming motive
practices.preview: Describe your experience without presenting the other person’s intention as fact.
lesson_cards: Your experience can be clear without claiming why the other person acted.
Name what happened and the effect it had on you or the decision.
Leave motive open unless the other person has actually stated it.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which sentence owns the speaker’s experience without claiming motive?
options: You leave it to me because you don’t respect my time.
When bedtime comes back to me after we split it, I feel like I’m still managing the whole routine.
feedback: A presents a motive as fact. B connects the event to the speaker’s experience.
B makes the impact visible without claiming intention.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: Are you saying I don’t care about your time?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Clarify your experience without claiming what the other person intended.

may_evaluate: Motive is not presented as fact.
may_not_infer: the learner’s emotional state beyond their words

retry.direction: Name what happened and its impact without claiming why the other person did it.

practices.transfer_cue: Separate the impact you know from the motive you are guessing.

practices.title: Give the opening one purpose
practices.preview: Make it clear what you want this conversation to do.
lesson_cards: An opening is easier to answer when it has one purpose.
Name the topic, one current example, and the decision or request.
Leave the rest of the history outside the opening.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which opening gives the conversation one purpose?
options: We need to discuss why this keeps happening and what it says about us.
Can we decide who owns bedtime Tuesday and Thursday? I handled it alone four nights this week.
feedback: A opens several jobs and a relationship verdict. B makes one decision visible.
B names the topic, current example, and one purpose.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What are you asking us to decide?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Give the opening one topic, one current example, and one purpose or request.

retry.direction: Use one topic, one current example, and one purpose or request.

practices.transfer_cue: Before the conversation, say the purpose of the opening in one sentence.

practices.title: Open clearly under mild pressure
practices.preview: Build one opener, then respond to one pushback without opening a second argument.
lesson_cards: Put the pieces into a single opener.
Say what you want settled, what happened, the point you want to keep clear, and what you’re asking for.
Then let the other person answer. If they push back, respond and return to the request.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which opener is easier to answer?
options: You always leave everything to me, and I’m tired of being the only adult who notices anything.
Can we talk about bedtime? I handled it alone four nights this week. Can you take Tuesday and Thursday, from pajamas through lights out?
feedback: A opens with a verdict on the person. B opens with a count, a point, and a question that can be answered.
B gives a specific week and a request that can be answered.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I don’t think it’s that serious.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Respond to the pushback without opening a second argument. Then return to your request.
preset_scenario.user_opening_objective: Say what you want settled, what happened, the point you want to keep clear, and your request.
approved_pushback_bank: I don’t think it’s that serious.
I’ve had a long day. Can this wait?
I thought we already handled this.

may_evaluate: One point and request remain identifiable.

retry.direction: Retry the coached segment, then use the same selected pushback.

branches.opener: Reset before the opener, capture the revised opener, then play the same selected pushback.
branches.pushback_response: Replay the same selected pushback, then capture the revised response.

practices.transfer_cue: Save one sentence from today’s practice for the real conversation.

modules.title: Listen and Respond
modules.promise: Understand what the other person actually said without immediately fixing, defending, correcting, or abandoning your own point.
modules.completion_capability: I can show what I heard before deciding whether to agree, clarify, disagree, or return to my point.

practices.title: Ask a question whose answer could matter
practices.preview: Ask before deciding you already know the explanation.
lesson_cards: A useful question leaves room for information you do not already have.
An accusation with a question mark is still an accusation.
Use a direct yes-or-no question when the conversation genuinely needs a decision.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which question could change or clarify what you understand?
options: Why do you never think about how this affects me?
What gets in the way of taking bedtime when you get home?
feedback: A assumes the answer and prosecutes it. B asks for information that could matter.
B asks for information without hiding an accusation inside the question.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: My schedule changes every week.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Ask one question before rebutting or proposing a solution.

may_evaluate: The answer could change or clarify understanding.

retry.direction: Ask one question whose answer you do not already assume.

practices.transfer_cue: Replace one anticipated motive with one real question in the next safe conversation.

source_lineage: former Day 10; V1.1 architecture approved, copy draft
practices.title: Say back the concern and check it
practices.preview: Respond to what was stated, then leave room to be corrected.
lesson_cards: Start with what the other person actually stated: a fact, constraint, priority, or request.
Say it back in your own words.
End as a check, not a verdict about what they really mean.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response reflects what was stated and leaves room for correction?
options: You always have an excuse.
The schedule uncertainty is the part making fixed nights hard. Is that right?
feedback: A replaces the stated constraint with a judgment. B reflects the constraint and checks it.
B stays with the stated concern and leaves room for correction.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: My schedule changes every week.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Reflect the stated constraint in your own words and check whether you have it right.

may_evaluate: The response is grounded in the stated words.

retry.direction: Reflect the stated concern in your own words, then check whether you have it right.

practices.transfer_cue: Before answering, name whether you heard a fact, constraint, priority, or request.

source_lineage: former Day 11; V1.1 architecture approved, copy draft
practices.title: When the concern is about you
practices.preview: Make contact with a specific complaint before defending or counterattacking.
lesson_cards: Receiving a complaint does not require agreeing with every detail.
Show what you heard before correcting, explaining, or raising your own complaint.
You can dispute facts after the specific concern has made contact.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response makes contact before defense?
options: That is not what happened, and you do it to me too.
You are saying the correction in front of the kids landed as talking down to you. Which moment do you mean?
feedback: A defends and counterattacks before touching the complaint. B shows what was heard and asks for the specific moment.
B makes contact with the complaint before deciding whether to agree or clarify.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: When you corrected me in front of the kids, I felt talked down to.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Respond to the specific complaint before explaining, correcting, or raising another issue.

may_evaluate: The specific complaint is acknowledged before defense.

retry.direction: Show what you heard before you explain, correct, or raise your own concern.

practices.transfer_cue: When the concern is about you, show what landed before deciding what you think about it.

practices.title: Acknowledge without pretending to agree
practices.preview: Name the understandable part while keeping factual or practical disagreement available.
lesson_cards: Validation means recognizing an understandable perspective or concern.
It does not require agreeing with every conclusion.
Name the part you can honestly acknowledge before adding the point that remains.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response acknowledges something real without pretending to agree?
options: I hear you, but you always say that when you do not want to decide.
I understand why fixed nights feel risky with your schedule. I still need us to decide how bedtime gets owned.
feedback: A uses acknowledgment as a runway for an accusation. B names the understandable constraint and preserves the decision.
B acknowledges a real concern without giving up the original point.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: Fixed nights are hard when my schedule keeps changing.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Acknowledge one understandable part, then preserve the decision or request.

may_evaluate: The original point may remain visible.

retry.direction: Name the understandable part first, then preserve the point in one sentence.

practices.transfer_cue: Look for one concern you can honestly acknowledge even when the decision remains open.

practices.title: Hear impact before explaining intent
practices.preview: Make contact with the impact you were told about before describing what you meant.
lesson_cards: Intent and impact can both matter.
Explaining intent first can make the described impact disappear.
Start with the impact you heard. Clarify intent after contact has been made.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response makes contact with impact first?
options: I did not mean to leave you alone, so that is not fair.
I hear that leaving without a return time left you alone with the whole problem.
feedback: A uses intent to dismiss the impact. B reflects the described impact first.
B makes contact with the impact without claiming more than was stated.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: When you left without saying when you would return, I felt alone with the whole problem.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Acknowledge the described impact before explaining what you intended.

may_evaluate: The described impact is acknowledged before intent.

retry.direction: Start with the impact you heard. Save intent for the next sentence or a later turn.

practices.transfer_cue: When intent defense appears, ask what impact the other person is trying to describe.

practices.title: Respond without losing your own point
practices.preview: Acknowledge what matters without following every new branch.
lesson_cards: Being responsive does not require following every branch.
Acknowledge the concern that belongs in the exchange.
Then return to the request, boundary, decision, or next step you started with.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response acknowledges and returns?
options: Okay, never mind. We can talk about my tone instead.
You are right that I sounded sharp. I want to address that, and I also want to finish deciding who owns bedtime.
feedback: A drops the original decision. B acknowledges the concern and keeps the decision visible.
B uses two moves: acknowledge once, then return.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: The way you brought this up was unfair.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Acknowledge the concern, then return to the original decision.

retry.direction: Acknowledge once, then return to the one decision.

practices.transfer_cue: Prepare one return phrase that sounds natural rather than scripted.

modules.title: Stay Clear Under Pushback
modules.promise: Keep the point when someone becomes defensive, minimizes, changes the subject, or pushes back.
modules.completion_capability: I can respond to resistance without attacking, proving everything, or abandoning the point.

practices.title: Spot what pressure makes you do
practices.preview: Notice the first move you make after someone pushes back.
lesson_cards: Pressure can change what you do next. That move is behavior, not a personality type.
You might talk faster, pile on proof, attack, go quiet, apologize your way out, or rush to fix it.
Listen for a move in your own recording. After Hope’s note, choose whether it fits what happened.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which one names a move instead of a type?
options: I’m just bad at conflict.
When I hear “you’re overreacting,” I start listing older examples.
feedback: A labels the person. B names the cue and the move that followed.
B names the cue and the move that followed it.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: Why is this suddenly such a big deal?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Answer the way you would actually answer, then review the first observable move you made.

may_evaluate: One exact observable move is identified.
The learner can confirm or reject whether it fits.

retry.direction: Answer the same objection. Change only the move Hope named.

practices.transfer_cue: Listen for the first thing you do after pushback.

learner_correction_state.rejection_policy: Do not preserve the observation as ground truth. Offer transcript correction or a neutral retry.

practices.title: Narrow the all-or-nothing frame
practices.preview: Clarify the specific concern without counterattacking or accepting a global accusation.
lesson_cards: Defensiveness can turn one concern into a claim about everything.
Clarify what you are not claiming.
Then restate the specific concern or request you are making now.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response narrows the frame?
options: There you go making yourself the victim again.
I am not saying you never help. I am talking about who owns bedtime on these two nights.
feedback: A counterattacks. B rejects the global frame and keeps the current scope visible.
B clarifies the scope without surrendering or expanding the accusation.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: So now everything is my fault?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Clarify the scope, then restate the current issue.

may_evaluate: The false global frame is narrowed.

retry.direction: Clarify what you are not claiming, then restate what you are asking now.

practices.transfer_cue: When an always-or-never defense appears, narrow the scope instead of expanding the case.

practices.title: Respond when the issue is minimized
practices.preview: Name why the issue matters without adding volume or history.
lesson_cards: More volume and more history rarely make a minimized issue clearer.
Name the current impact once.
Then return to the request or decision.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response preserves importance without building a case?
options: It is a big deal, and here are twelve reasons you never understand me.
It may feel small to you. For me, it determines whether I get predictable recovery time, so I still want a clear plan.
feedback: A adds volume and history. B names one impact and returns to the plan.
B explains why it matters without requiring the other person to feel the same weight.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: This is not that big a deal.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Use one impact sentence and return to the request.

retry.direction: Use one impact sentence and one request. Do not add another example.

practices.transfer_cue: When minimized, state why it matters to you without demanding equal emotional weight.

practices.title: Handle a counterattack without opening two arguments
practices.preview: Give a second issue a real return point, then finish the first job.
lesson_cards: A new concern can be legitimate and still derail the current decision.
Acknowledge it and choose an order.
A real return point is different from dismissing it or arguing about both at once.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response gives both issues an order?
options: Fine. Let us talk about everything you do wrong too.
I am willing to talk about that next. Can we finish the bedtime decision first, then take your concern?
feedback: A opens both arguments. B acknowledges the second concern and gives it a return point.
B protects the current job without dismissing the second issue.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: You keep criticizing my tone, but you interrupt me all the time.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Acknowledge the second issue, give it a return point, and finish the first job.

may_evaluate: A credible return point is offered.

retry.direction: Acknowledge the second issue, give it a return point, then finish the first job.

practices.transfer_cue: Use a brief parking place for a second issue rather than debating both at once.

practices.title: Respond to vague agreement or refusal
practices.preview: Choose a next move that fits instead of treating persistence as success.
lesson_cards: Not every response needs another argument.
A vague yes may need clarification; a real no may need acceptance, negotiation, a boundary, or an ending.
Choose the next move based on the conversation job, authority, and safety.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response treats refusal as information instead of automatic failure?
options: We cannot stop until you agree.
We do not agree tonight. Let us name what remains open and decide whether there is a legitimate next step.
feedback: A forces agreement. B names the current reality and leaves room for an appropriate next step.
B does not confuse persistence with skill.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I am not agreeing to fixed nights.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Choose whether to clarify, negotiate, accept the no, pause, or name an appropriate boundary.

may_evaluate: The response fits the stated refusal and the learner’s authority.

retry.direction: Name the current reality and choose one legitimate next step without forcing agreement.

practices.transfer_cue: Before a difficult conversation, identify which endings would still count as skillful.

blocked_practices.title: Choose a response you were not prompted to use
blocked_practices.technical_gate: Requires a larger reaction bank, identical controlled retry, and separately labeled varied-reaction transfer state.

modules.title: Pause, Say No, or Set a Boundary
modules.promise: Slow or end a conversation cleanly, make a real boundary, and stop treating every disagreement as something that must be resolved immediately.
modules.completion_capability: I can pause, decline, set a limit, or end without disappearing, threatening, or forcing agreement.

practices.title: Create enough space to choose
practices.preview: Take a moment after pushback, then pick one thing to say.
lesson_cards: You don’t have to feel calm. Take enough time to choose what you say next.
After an objection, pick one move. Say a sentence, ask a question, or ask to come back to it.
Adding more words before you choose usually hides the move you meant to make.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which one leaves room to choose?
options: No, listen, because last week you also, and the week before that…
(brief pause) The main thing I’m asking is whether you can own Tuesday bedtime.
feedback: A keeps adding evidence. B waits, then says one thing.
B waits, then makes one move the other person can answer.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I don’t see why we need a schedule. We’ve been figuring it out.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Take a moment. Then say one sentence, ask one question, or ask to come back to it.

may_evaluate: The response does not pile on evidence.
The move is answerable or usable.
may_not_infer: intentional silence from recording latency or speech difference

retry.direction: Take a moment after the objection. Then make one move.

practices.transfer_cue: When you catch yourself piling on words, stop there and pick one thing to say.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

practices.title: Ask for a pause with a return
practices.preview: Pause the conversation without making it disappear.
lesson_cards: A useful pause names that the conversation is stopping for now.
Add a return time or readiness condition and say who will restart.
A pause is not a punishment, threat, or indefinite disappearance.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which pause contains a return?
options: I cannot do this. I am done.
I need to pause. I will come back at 8:30 after bedtime and restart this.
feedback: A stops without a return. B names the pause, return time, and restart owner.
B protects the conversation without requiring it to continue now.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: If we stop now, this is never going to get resolved.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Request a pause and name when or under what condition you will restart.

may_evaluate: A credible return condition is present.

retry.direction: Name the pause, the return condition, and who will restart.

practices.transfer_cue: Use a pause only when appropriate, state the return, and follow through.
safety_contract: Do not prescribe a return when direct conversation is unsafe.
Do not universalize a twenty-minute pause.

practices.title: Receive a pause without chasing
practices.preview: Accept another person’s pause while making the return visible.
lesson_cards: Receiving a pause does not require accepting indefinite disappearance.
Acknowledge the need to stop, then ask for a credible return condition.
Do not use pressure, pursuit, or catastrophe to force the conversation to continue.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response accepts the pause and protects the return?
options: No. We are finishing this now.
Okay. When should we check back, and who will restart?
feedback: A refuses the pause. B accepts it and asks for a return contract.
B leaves room to stop while keeping the issue from silently disappearing.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I need to stop. I cannot keep talking right now.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Accept the pause and ask for a return condition without chasing or collapsing.

may_evaluate: The response does not force immediate continuation.

retry.direction: Accept the pause, then ask for a credible return condition.

practices.transfer_cue: When someone asks to pause, protect both the stop and the return.
safety_contract: Do not pressure a return when credible safety or retaliation concerns exist.
Do not interpret a pause request as abandonment.

practices.title: Know whether this is a request or a boundary
practices.preview: Separate what you are asking them to do from what you will do.
lesson_cards: A request asks what the other person will do.
A boundary states what you will do when a real limit is crossed.
A threat uses punishment or fear to force compliance.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which statement is controlled by the speaker?
options: You have to stop insulting me or else.
If insults start again, I will pause and return when we can speak without them.
feedback: A demands control without naming the speaker’s action. B states the action the speaker will take.
B connects a user-controlled action to a real limit.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: You are overreacting. We are finishing this conversation.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: State the limit and the action you will take if it continues.

may_evaluate: The action is controlled by the learner.
The consequence is connected to the limit.

retry.direction: State what you will do, not what you will force them to do.

practices.transfer_cue: Use a boundary only where a real limit exists; do not turn every preference into one.
safety_contract: Do not coach direct boundary announcement when credible coercion, violence, stalking, or retaliation is disclosed.

practices.title: Say no without a hostile essay
practices.preview: Decline clearly without inventing excuses or prosecuting the request.
lesson_cards: A clear no does not need a long defense.
Give a brief reason only when it is useful and safe.
Declining a request does not require attacking the person who asked.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which refusal is clear without opening another argument?
options: No, because you always ask at the worst time and never think about me.
No, I cannot take that on this week.
feedback: A turns the refusal into a prosecution. B gives a clear answer without a new case.
B is direct and leaves the request answered.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: Can you take over both school drop-off and pickup this week?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Decline the request clearly without inventing an excuse or attacking the person.

may_evaluate: No unnecessary counterattack or invented excuse is added.
may_not_infer: whether the refusal is morally correct

retry.direction: Give a clear no. Add only the reason or alternative that actually matters.

practices.transfer_cue: Practice one concise no before a lower-stakes request where declining is legitimate.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

practices.title: Accept no without forcing resolution
practices.preview: Respond to a refusal without treating persistence as proof of good communication.
lesson_cards: A no is information, not automatic evidence that the request was badly communicated.
You may clarify, negotiate an alternative, name your own boundary, or accept the refusal.
Do not turn the answer into a test of love, loyalty, or character.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response treats no as information?
options: If you cared, you would find a way.
Okay. Is there another arrangement you can commit to, or should I plan without this?
feedback: A converts refusal into a care test. B asks one legitimate follow-up and allows the no to remain real.
B keeps the practical need visible without forcing agreement.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: No. I cannot commit to either night.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Choose one fitting response: clarify, ask for an alternative, accept the no, or state a real boundary.

may_evaluate: The counterpart is not pressured into agreement.
may_not_infer: which consequence is safe without context

retry.direction: Respond to the no without turning agreement into a test of care.

practices.transfer_cue: Before asking, decide what you will do if the answer is no.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

practices.title: Choose the right ending
practices.preview: End with the reality that exists instead of forcing resolution.
lesson_cards: Agreement is only one possible ending.
Other endings include disagreement, pause, revisit, boundary, support, documentation, escalation, or exit.
The ending should fit the conversation job, authority, and safety.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which ending names reality without forcing agreement?
options: We cannot stop until you admit I am right.
We do not agree tonight. Let us revisit the schedule Sunday after we check our commitments.
feedback: A forces resolution. B names the disagreement and a legitimate next step.
B treats unresolved disagreement as a possible ending.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: I am not changing my answer tonight.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Name the current reality and one legitimate next step, including no further conversation when appropriate.

may_evaluate: The ending fits the stated situation.
Agreement is not treated as the only successful outcome.

retry.direction: Name the current reality and one legitimate next step without forcing agreement.

practices.transfer_cue: Before a real conversation, identify which endings would still count as skillful.
safety_contract: Safety routing may replace ordinary closure with support, documentation, formal escalation, or exit.

blocked_practices.title: Reclaim one bounded sentence after interruption
blocked_practices.technical_gate: Requires honest interruption or barge-in during an active learner turn, reliable timing, transcript segmentation, and safe duplex audio behavior. A post-recording clip is not an interruption.

modules.title: Repair What Went Wrong
modules.promise: Own what you said or did badly without erasing the issue that still needs attention.
modules.completion_capability: I can own the miss, name what I will change, and reopen the real issue without using it as an excuse.

practices.title: Name the specific miss
practices.preview: Identify the action or delivery problem instead of apologizing for everything.
lesson_cards: A useful repair starts with the specific thing that happened.
Name the words, action, or delivery problem.
Do not turn the repair into a global judgment about yourself.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which repair names the specific miss?
options: I am sorry I am such a terrible partner.
I raised my voice and called you selfish.
feedback: A turns the repair into a global self-judgment. B names the behavior that needs repair.
B gives the other person a specific action to respond to.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What exactly are you apologizing for?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Name the specific words, action, or delivery problem.

may_evaluate: A specific repair target is identifiable.

retry.direction: Name the specific words, action, or delivery problem without judging your whole character.

practices.transfer_cue: When repair is needed, name the bounded miss before explaining anything else.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

practices.title: Own it without “but”
practices.preview: Take responsibility without using the underlying issue as a justification.
lesson_cards: The original issue may still matter. It does not excuse harmful delivery.
Own the specific behavior before reopening the issue.
A “but” inside the apology usually turns ownership back into blame.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which statement owns the miss without making it the other person’s fault?
options: I am sorry I yelled, but you pushed me there.
I raised my voice and called you selfish. That was unfair.
feedback: A makes the other person responsible for the behavior. B owns it directly.
B names and owns the behavior without adding a justification.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: Are you saying this was my fault too?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Own the behavior without adding a justification or counter-blame.

may_evaluate: The learner owns the behavior without qualification.

retry.direction: Remove the justification. Own the specific behavior in one sentence.

practices.transfer_cue: Listen for “but” after an apology and separate the repair from the unresolved issue.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

practices.title: Acknowledge the impact you were told about
practices.preview: Make contact with described impact without pretending to know more than was said.
lesson_cards: Repair includes the impact the other person actually described.
Use their stated experience rather than inventing what they must have felt.
You can acknowledge impact without agreeing to facts that remain disputed.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response acknowledges stated impact without mind-reading?
options: I know I destroyed your trust completely.
You said the name-calling made it harder to talk about the actual problem.
feedback: A invents a total relationship outcome. B stays with the impact that was stated.
B acknowledges the described impact without claiming more than the evidence supports.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: The name-calling made me stop listening to the actual issue.
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Acknowledge the impact that was stated without adding an inferred feeling or outcome.

may_evaluate: No unspoken impact is presented as fact.

retry.direction: Acknowledge the impact you were told about without adding an outcome they did not state.

practices.transfer_cue: In a repair, use the impact that was described rather than the one you imagine.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

practices.title: Say what will be different next time
practices.preview: Make the repair actionable by naming one behavior you will change.
lesson_cards: An apology describes the miss. Repair also names what changes next.
Choose one behavior under your control.
Do not promise a personality transformation or a perfect future.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which statement names an observable change?
options: I promise I will be a better communicator.
If I start labeling you, I will stop and return to one request.
feedback: A promises a broad identity change. B names a behavior the speaker can perform.
B makes the next behavior visible and controllable.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What will you do differently when we restart?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Name one observable behavior you will use instead.

may_evaluate: One changed behavior is observable and controlled by the learner.

retry.direction: Name one behavior you will use instead when the same pressure appears.

practices.transfer_cue: A repair becomes credible through the next observable action, not a bigger promise.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

practices.title: Reopen the issue without using it as an excuse
practices.preview: Return to the legitimate concern only after the repair has made contact.
lesson_cards: Repair does not require abandoning the issue underneath it.
Finish the ownership before reopening the concern.
Reopen with one point or request, not a renewed prosecution.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which response repairs first and then reopens the issue?
options: I should not have yelled, but the bedtime problem is still your fault.
Calling you selfish was unfair. I want to restart and make one clear request about bedtime.
feedback: A uses the issue to qualify the repair. B completes ownership and then reopens with one purpose.
B keeps repair and the underlying issue separate enough for both to remain visible.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: Are you apologizing, or are you trying to restart the argument?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Complete the ownership, then reopen with one point or request.

may_evaluate: The underlying issue is reopened as one discussable point.

retry.direction: Finish the ownership first. Then reopen with one point or request.

practices.transfer_cue: When you reopen, demonstrate the changed behavior instead of repeating the original delivery.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

gated_practices.title: Let follow-through complete the repair
gated_practices.teaching_contract: Review whether the learner completed the specific changed behavior they selected, without inferring forgiveness or relationship repair.
gated_practices.technical_gate: Requires persisted repair commitment, later check-in state, no-action branch, and adverse-event/safety routing.

modules.title: Use It in Real Life
modules.promise: Combine the skills, prepare for a real conversation, review what happened, and build a personal playbook.
modules.completion_capability: I can select and apply the right behavior in a realistic situation rather than rely on one memorized script.

practices.title: Choose conditions that can hold the conversation
practices.preview: Select a safe time, place, channel, and scope before rehearsing the plan.
lesson_cards: The same words can land differently depending on timing, privacy, channel, and power.
Choose conditions that can hold the job you want the conversation to do.
Delay, document, seek support, or do not proceed when direct conversation is not appropriate.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which plan chooses usable conditions?
options: I will bring it up in the car when neither of us can leave.
I will ask after bedtime when we have privacy, and I will move it to writing if timing changes.
feedback: A removes choice and safe exit. B names usable conditions and an alternative channel.
B makes timing, privacy, and an alternate channel visible.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: When and how do you want to have this conversation?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Name a safe time, place, channel, and alternate route.

may_evaluate: A safe alternate route is available when needed.

retry.direction: Choose a safer time, place, channel, or alternate route for the same conversation.

practices.transfer_cue: Before a real conversation, check timing, privacy, channel, and whether direct conversation is appropriate.
safety_contract: Credible fear, coercion, retaliation, legal sensitivity, or danger routes away from ordinary rehearsal.

practices.title: Choose one goal under your control
practices.preview: Decide what behavior you want available even if the other person does not agree.
lesson_cards: An outcome goal depends on both people. A process goal names what you will do.
Choose one behavior you want available at the hardest moment.
Agreement may happen, but it cannot be the skill the app asks you to control.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which goal is controlled by the learner?
options: Make them finally understand and agree.
State one request and return to it after one objection.
feedback: A requires the other person’s agreement. B names behavior the learner can perform.
B remains measurable even if the counterpart disagrees.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What do you want to be able to do when the conversation gets difficult?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Name one process goal under your control.

may_evaluate: One observable learner behavior is identified.

retry.direction: Name one behavior you want available regardless of the other person’s answer.

practices.transfer_cue: Before the conversation, choose one behavior you can control instead of an outcome you cannot.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

practices.title: Build one if–then response
practices.preview: Connect one likely cue to one behavior you have practiced.
lesson_cards: A plan is easier to use when it links a cue to one response.
Name the pressure moment you expect, then the behavior you will try.
Keep the plan specific enough to rehearse and flexible enough to say in your own words.

discrimination_check.prompt: Which plan connects one cue to one observable response?
options: If it goes badly, I will communicate better.
If the conversation shifts to everything I do wrong, I will give that issue a return point and finish the bedtime decision first.
feedback: A does not name the cue or behavior. B links one likely cue to a practiced response.
B creates a response that can be rehearsed before the real moment.

preset_scenario.counterpart_turn: What reaction are you most likely to hear?
preset_scenario.user_response_objective: Complete one plan: If this cue happens, then I will use this behavior.

may_evaluate: One cue and one observable response are present.

retry.direction: Use one specific cue and one behavior you can perform when it appears.

practices.transfer_cue: Save one if–then plan for the moment most likely to pull you off your point.
safety_contract: Ordinary rehearsal stops when credible fear, coercion, retaliation, or danger is disclosed.

gated_practices.title: Use the plan or choose a high-fidelity rehearsal
gated_practices.teaching_contract: The learner chooses whether and when to attempt the real conversation; postponing or declining is not failure. A saved-scenario rehearsal is always available.
gated_practices.technical_gate: Requires persisted plan, user-selected window, no-conversation branch, adverse-event capture, and safety routing.

blocked_practices.title: Rehearse a different plausible reaction
blocked_practices.technical_gate: Requires separate controlled-retry and varied-transfer attempt types so the second stimulus cannot contaminate comparison.

blocked_practices.title: Review what actually happened
blocked_practices.technical_gate: Requires saved plan, did-not-happen branch, user/counterpart/outcome separation, adverse-event capture, and safety review.

blocked_practices.title: Replay the hardest moment with one adjustment
blocked_practices.technical_gate: Requires a confirmed debrief moment and a deterministic reconstruction that does not claim the simulation is the real conversation.

blocked_practices.title: Build a playbook from choices you made
blocked_practices.technical_gate: Every item must be learner-authored or explicitly selected; Hope may use consented exact quotes but may not infer frequency, personality, or patterns.

blocked_practices.title: Apply the skill in a new scenario
blocked_practices.technical_gate: Requires novel comparable-scenario state, an unprompted first attempt, stable reaction identity, and separate transfer evidence.

blocked_practices.title: Compare with the preserved baseline
blocked_practices.technical_gate: Requires durable uncoached onboarding artifact, matched-condition metadata, condition-aware comparison, and a separately validated multi-dimension contract.
